To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

novice users are more concerned with the attractiveness of an e-service and its ease of use and ease of understanding; novice users associate information quality with the amount of information provided and the ease of finding it; novice users are more likely to perceive an e-service as having a good reputation if the organization providing it is perceived as having a good one.
novice users are more likely to use e-services that are easy to use, easy to understand, and have a good reputation.
novice users perceive e-services that are more attractive and easier to use and understand, as being of higher quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of e-service quality for novice users, which is a critical factor in e-service proliferation.
the following question: How do novice users perceive e-services?
how novice users perceive e-services and the implications of their perception for e-service design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study indicate that novice users perceive the e-services more highly in terms on usability and information quality.

novice users are not only interested in the quality of the services they receive but also in their ease of use and the attractiveness of the service presentation, which are the two main dimensions that novice users focus on.
the novice users' perceptions of e-service are influenced by the design of the service and their previous experience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
novice users' perception of e-services is affected by their experience with the organization and with the internet, and by the design of the e-service.
novice users are attracted to simple, attractive, easy to learn e-services, but are willing to accept more complex interactions for the sake of information quality.
we are trying to find out what novice users perceive as good e-services.
The main takeaway from our work is that
novice users are not as concerned as experienced users about the quality of e-services.
novice users are a distinct user group and that e-service design should take their needs into account.
e-services should focus on the novice user, who is likely to have a more positive perception of the e-service than an experienced user.
